content.text: I'm thinking through how to approach this.

Schematic of the residual-based intercept correction workflow on five synthetic observations. Baseline predictions 2x and observed targets y determine residuals r_i, from which the scalar correction b = 3 is computed. Adding b yields corrected predictions 2x + b, which achieve zero error when evaluated on the same observations. The dashed path highlights observation reuse, reflecting an exact finite arithmetic verification rather than out-of-sample generalization.
Schematic of the residual-based intercept correction workflow on five synthetic observations. Baseline predictions 2x and
observed targets y determine the residuals r_i, from which the mean correction b = 3 is computed. Adding this
scalar offset produces corrected predictions 2x + b, which evaluate to zero residual error on the original data. The dashed
path highlights the reuse of the five observations, underscoring that this procedure represents an exact finite arithmetic verification rather than predictive generalization.
